title: Equity vs Cash
hook: A paycheck gets spent. Ownership keeps growing while you sleep.
statement: Ownership compounds, labor doesn't. Owning assets builds wealth that cash income alone never will.
explainer: Cash gets spent and it's gone. Equity in your business, property, or investments keeps growing. If none of your income turns into ownership, you're running in place.
sop: List your income sources and mark each as cash or equity.
Figure out what share of this month's income went into owning things.
Add up your Assets and Liabilities for a real net worth number.
Redirect one recurring cash expense into an equity move next month.
Review quarterly to see if your equity is actually growing.
equation_example: Assets $150,000, Liabilities $40,000. $150,000 minus $40,000 = $110,000 net worth. Rising means you're building wealth that compounds. Flat or falling means income is getting spent as fast as it comes in.
question: Write down your net worth today. Real numbers, not a guess.
closing_statement: Own things that grow, not just money that gets spent.
caption:
Principle Nº 172: Equity vs Cash
